assumptions.ruleset: Gathering Storm with every expansion and the Leader Pass
assumptions.map: Continents or Small Continents, standard size, 8 civilizations
assumptions.notes: Turn numbers are Standard-speed scaffolding; the site rescales them for other speeds and difficulties. Hojo Tokimune's single persona is planned here, not Tokugawa. The shape is Front-Load because the city spacing and the order districts are placed in are decided before the second Settler and cannot be undone; the kit itself is flat and works on almost any start.

verdict.one_line: Settle cities three tiles apart along the coast, pin a four-district cluster in each before anything is built, and let half-price Theater Squares and Holy Sites plus full adjacency from every neighbouring district carry a Culture game that the Electronics Factory finishes.
verdict.why: Meiji Restoration turns district adjacency from a terrain problem into a geometry problem: a Theater Square touching three districts has +3 before any wonder or river, in every city, on any map. Divine Wind halves the cost of exactly the districts a Culture game is built on, Theater Squares and Holy Sites, and the Faith from cheap Holy Sites buys the Great Writers, Artists and Musicians that fill them. The Electronics Factory adds Culture to every city within six tiles, which a tightly spaced empire means every city. Science is the secondary because Campuses in the same clusters get the same adjacency, not because the kit points there. Domination is possible on a coast with Samurai but it spends the half-price districts on nothing.

must_have: Flat or hill land for at least four cities three tiles apart, each with room for a four-district cluster, within 12 tiles of the capital.
Nothing else. The kit is terrain-independent; the check is about spacing, not features.
prefer: A coastal capital, so Harbors join the clusters, Divine Wind defends the shore, and Seaside Resorts pay Tourism later.
Hills under the capital and the first two cities for Production; the districts are cheap but there are many of them.
A river or coast running past three sites, for Commercial Hub and Harbor adjacency on top of the district adjacency.
Woods and coast near the cluster sites for appeal: National Parks and Seaside Resorts are the late Tourism.
map_check.no_go: A start hemmed in by mountains, marsh or a rival within six tiles so that fewer than three cities fit at three-tile spacing. The kit then has no clusters to multiply and Japan is an ordinary civ with a cheap Encampment.
map_check.fallback: Settle in place and play Japan as a one-city-cluster Culture civ: capital plus two satellites at the closest legal spacing, Theater Square and Holy Site in each, and take a neighbour's nearest city with Samurai around turn 120 to make a fourth. Say the empire will be small and plan Tourism from wonders and Seaside Resorts rather than from city count.

kit_levers.name: Divine Wind
kit_levers.buys: Five Combat Strength for land units on tiles beside Coast and for naval units in shallow water, and Encampments, Holy Sites and Theater Squares built in half the time.
kit_levers.exploit: Every city builds a Theater Square and a Holy Site as its first two districts because they cost half; the Campus and Commercial Hub come third and fourth at full price with the adjacency the first two give them. The combat bonus means the empire is defended by the coast it settled, not by an army.

kit_levers.name: Meiji Restoration
kit_levers.buys: Every district gets a full +1 adjacency from each adjacent district instead of the half point other civilizations get.
kit_levers.exploit: Districts are placed in a ring that touches the City Center and each other, never spread to chase a mountain or a river. The order matters: the first district placed has no neighbours yet, so it is the Holy Site or Theater Square, which are cheap; the Campus goes in once two districts already border its tile.

kit_levers.name: Samurai
kit_levers.buys: A Medieval melee unit that fights at full strength however damaged it is, with no Iron requirement.
kit_levers.exploit: Not an offensive plan. Four Samurai on coastal tiles with Divine Wind hold the whole shore against a Renaissance invasion, which lets the empire skip Walls in the inner cities and keep Production on districts. If a neighbour's coastal city is weak around turn 120, the same four take it.

kit_levers.name: Electronics Factory
kit_levers.buys: A Factory that also gives Culture to every city within six tiles once Electricity is researched.
kit_levers.exploit: With cities three tiles apart, one Electronics Factory covers four or five cities. Two Industrial Zones, placed at the ends of the cluster chain, cover the empire; the Culture they add is the late push into the civics that unlock Tourism cards.

kit_levers.name: Bushido
kit_levers.buys: Tokimune likes civilizations with a strong military and high Faith and Culture, and dislikes a strong military without them.
kit_levers.exploit: Irrelevant to your own play. An AI Hojo on the map will respect a Culture civ with a standing army, so keeping four Samurai is diplomacy as well as defence.

turn_zero: Before the Settler moves: can three more cities sit exactly three tiles from this spot and from each other, each with four flat or hill tiles in its first ring free for districts? Count them on the visible map. Three or more: settle. Fewer: move one turn toward open land, then settle whatever is there.
Before the Settler moves: is the capital coastal? If coast is one move away, take it; Harbors join the clusters, Divine Wind defends them, and the first Seaside Resort tiles are decided now.

Before the Settler moves: pin the capital's cluster. Holy Site first on the tile that touches the center and two other future district tiles, Theater Square second touching both, Campus third touching both of those, Commercial Hub or Harbor fourth. Nothing is queued in the capital on any pinned tile.
By turn 10: write the order the clusters will be built in for the first four cities. The cheap districts go first everywhere because they create the adjacency the expensive ones collect.
front_load.ceiling: Eight to ten cities at three-tile spacing, each with four or five districts at +3 or more adjacency, each capped around 12 to 15 population by the tiles the spacing leaves them. That is a Culture victory around turn 280 on Emperor from Great Works, two wonder clusters and Seaside Resorts, with Science close behind. The cap is population: a tightly spaced Japan cannot run the 25-population cities a Science victory wants, so the Spaceport is the fallback and not the aim.

irreversibles.decision: Capital tile, which fixes the spacing grid for every later city; every site is measured three tiles from it.
Capital cluster pinned: which tile holds the Holy Site, which the Theater Square, which the Campus. A district placed off the pins breaks the adjacency of the other three.

The spacing plan for cities two through six, drawn before the second Settler finishes. Any city founded four or more tiles out loses the shared adjacency and the Electronics Factory coverage for good.
The build order of each cluster: Holy Site or Theater Square first in every city. A Campus placed first in a city has no neighbours and never gets its full adjacency back.
Which two cities hold the Industrial Zones for the Electronics Factories; the six-tile radius must cover every other city.

front_load.settle_map_rule: Draw every city two through eight before the second Settler is produced, on a grid of exactly three tiles between centers, following the coast where there is one. Each site must have four tiles in its first ring that are not resources, not mountains and not water, pinned as Holy Site, Theater Square, Campus and the fourth district. Cities seven and eight may be 40 turns away; they are drawn now so that cities three and four do not take their tiles. A site that cannot hold four districts at three tiles is skipped, not pushed out to four.

phases.name: Assess and commit
phases.objective: Settle on the grid, pin the capital's four-district cluster, draw the spacing plan for the next five cities, found the pantheon, and have the second Settler and the first Holy Site queued by turn 20. Every decision that caps this game is made in these twenty turns.

build_order.why: Finds the coastline, the first rival and three city-states; confirms the drawn sites are really there.
A second Warrior rather than a Slinger: with Divine Wind it holds the coast and clears the first camp for Military Tradition.
City two, three tiles along the coast; Magnus is not yet available so the capital pays the population.
Culture is the resource this plan spends; Early Empire and Political Philosophy on time.
Three improvements for Craftsmanship, Fishing Boats for Celestial Navigation, a Mine for The Wheel.
First district, half price, on the pinned tile; it starts the adjacency the Theater Square and Campus collect.
City three, three tiles the other way; both satellites exist before the capital's second district.
Second district once Drama and Poetry lands, half price, touching the Holy Site and the center.

research.note: First, for the half-price Holy Site; Eureka only if the Scout finds a natural wonder.
Mines on hills; the Production the many districts need.
Free from the coastal capital; Harbors are on this line.
Three camp kills with the coastal Warriors; Encampment at half price later.
Free from the first civilization met; the Campus goes third in every cluster.

civics.note: God King for the pantheon; Urban Planning once it is founded.
Inspiration from the first Builder; Ilkum for more Builders.
A Trader between the capital and city two; Inspiration if the Scout sees a second continent.

policies.why: The pantheon by turn 20 before the Holy Site exists.
Two Warriors on the coast with Divine Wind clear the camp.
Builders faster; every city needs Mines before its third district.

districts.note: First district on the pinned tile; half price; it is the anchor of the cluster.

pantheon.why: Every new city builds its first district a quarter faster, and this plan founds eight cities that each start with a district.

city_states.why: The first envoy is Culture in the capital toward Political Philosophy.

checkpoints.test: Capital settled with three sites at three-tile spacing visible, its four district tiles pinned, and the Scout along the coast?
checkpoints.pass: Continue; the spacing plan for cities two through six is drawn before the Settler finishes.
checkpoints.fail: Fewer than three legal sites: run the fallback and plan a three-city cluster. Pins missing: place them before the Holy Site is queued.

checkpoints.test: Second Settler out, Astrology in, the Holy Site queued on its pin, and cities two through six drawn with their clusters?
checkpoints.pass: Enter the cluster phase and follow the map.
checkpoints.fail: No map yet: draw it this turn, before the Settler moves. Holy Site queued off its pin: cancel it; the Production is refunded and the adjacency is not.

tasks.text: Settle on the coast if it is within one move; count the three-tile sites before the Settler plants.
Pin Holy Site, Theater Square, Campus and Commercial Hub or Harbor in the capital's first ring, touching each other and the center.
Scout along the coast both ways; mark camps, city-states and the sites the map drew.
Draw cities two through eight on the three-tile grid, each with four district tiles pinned, and write the cluster build order for each.
Found City Patron Goddess, or God of the Sea if the capital works four or more sea tiles.
Queue the capital Holy Site on its pin the turn Astrology completes.

phases.name: Build the clusters
phases.objective: Settle cities two through six on the grid and build each cluster in the pinned order: Holy Site, Theater Square, Campus, then the fourth district. Found a religion from the cheap Holy Sites so Faith can buy Great People later. Low decision density by design; the work is following the map.

build_order.why: Cities four, five and six on the grid; Colonization and Magnus Provision.
First in every new city; half price; the anchor.
Second in every city; half price; Amphitheater for the Great Writers.
Third in the capital and city two, touching both cheap districts; Recorded History at two.
Two Holy Sites with Shrines reach a Great Prophet before turn 80 on Emperor.
Great Writer points and the first Great Work slots.
Fourth district in coastal cities; Cartography at two; Trade Routes for Currency and Medieval Faires.
Mines on every hill in every city; the clusters are cheap, the buildings are not.

research.note: Two Fishing Boats; Harbors as the fourth district.
The first Trade Route; Commercial Hubs where there is no coast.
A Quarry if Stone is near; otherwise unboosted on the way to Construction.
Three different districts by turn 40 is free; Education follows for the Universities.
A Water Mill in the river city; Games and Recreation Inspiration comes with it.
A Mine on a resource; Water Mill.
Ancient Walls in the capital only; Eureka from building them.
Three Mines across the clusters; Industrial Zones later for the Electronics Factories.

checkpoints.fail: A city founded off the grid: it stays, but no further city leaves the grid and its cluster is drawn around what it has. No religion in reach: buy the second Shrine and keep God King one more turn.

phases.objective: The clusters finish and the yields compound: Universities, Art Museums ready for Great Artists, Markets and Harbors for Guilds and Medieval Faires, and the two Industrial Zones placed at the ends of the chain. Four Samurai hold the coast and nothing else is built for war.

decision_triggers.name: A site does not fit the grid
decision_triggers.if: The next planned city would have to sit four or more tiles from its neighbours to find flat land.
decision_triggers.then: Skip the site and take the next one on the grid, even if it is worse land. A city off the grid loses the shared adjacency and the Electronics Factory coverage for the rest of the game; a worse tile loses two Food.

decision_triggers.name: A neighbour lands on the coast
decision_triggers.if: A rival army disembarks beside any coastal city.
decision_triggers.then: Do not build Walls. Move the Samurai onto coastal tiles between the landing and the city; Divine Wind gives them five Strength and the city's own ranged attack finishes what they wound.

decision_triggers.name: Culture outruns Science
decision_triggers.if: At turn 150 the civics tree is two eras ahead of the techs.
decision_triggers.then: Normal for this plan. Slot Rationalism and Natural Philosophy, put Pingala on Researcher for twenty turns, and keep Culture first; do not add Campuses that break a cluster.

decision_triggers.name: The weak coastal city
decision_triggers.if: Around turn 120 a neighbour's coastal city within six tiles of your border has no Walls and two or fewer defenders.
decision_triggers.then: Take it with the four Samurai and keep it as a ninth city; pin its cluster the turn it is captured. One city only; the plan does not become a war.

abort.trigger: Turn 80 with fewer than four cities on the grid, or three or more clusters built out of order so that the Campuses and Theater Squares sit at +1 adjacency.
actions: Stop founding cities off the grid; what exists is the empire, and the plan says so.
Play a generic Culture game from wonders and Great Works: Apadana, Kilwa, the Forbidden City and the Hermitage in the capital, Faith-bought Great Artists.
Keep the four Samurai and consider the weak-coastal-city trigger to add a city the clusters could not.

fail_state: Turn 150 with cities four and five tiles apart, Theater Squares placed first where they touch nothing, two Industrial Zones that cover half the empire, and Culture in the middle of the table. The spacing decisions that caused it were made before turn 40 and no district can be moved.
common_mistakes: Placing the Campus first because it is the strongest district. It is placed third, once two cheap districts border its tile; placed first it has no neighbours and never gets them back.
Spreading cities to four tiles for better land. The adjacency and the Electronics Factory radius are the kit; the land is not.
Letting a wonder take a pinned district tile. Wonders go in the second ring; pins are districts.
Building Walls in every city because a neighbour looks aggressive. Divine Wind and four Samurai on the coast are the defence; Walls are Production taken from a Theater Square.
Treating Faith as a religion resource. The cheap Holy Sites exist to buy Great Writers, Artists, Musicians and Rock Bands; Apostles are not in this plan.
sources: Civilization VI Civilopedia, Gathering Storm ruleset (Japan, Hojo Tokimune, Samurai, Electronics Factory, Divine Wind, Meiji Restoration).

The civ-info text describes the Samurai as a Man-At-Arms replacement; in Gathering Storm it unlocks at Military Tactics with no Iron requirement, and the plan uses that. The Electronics Factory's Culture to cities within six tiles requires Electricity to be researched.
